usage.[current instance] [command]: Console runs the current executable file with parameters passed in, executes a single command but does not start interactive mode
usage.[current instance] -r \"[command1];[comm: The console runs the current executable file with the parameter - r, sequentially traverses and executes the incoming commands, executes multiple commands without starting interactive mode
usage.[current instance] [--cd-script|--cd-hom: Override startup working directory (cwd): --cd-script changes to script dir; --cd-home changes to HOME; --no-cd keeps current dir
Batch mode supports the same cwd flags; if not specified, command-line mode defaults to script dir

help.name: CMD
help.msg: cmd	(run system shell commands / open system shell)

usage.cmd: Enter the system shell interactively (type exit to return to Dox)
usage.cmd [command]: Run a single system command and echo its output, e.g. cmd dir
usage.cmd --timeout [seconds] [command]: Set the execution timeout; default 60 seconds, 0 means unlimited
usage.cmd ping -n 2 127.0.0.1: Example: run a system command with its own arguments (flags after the command are not consumed)

usage.help: Show detailed information about all commands
usage.help [command]: Show detailed information about specific command

help.msg: ?	(convert natural language to a command and execute)

usage.? [prompt]: Send prompt to AI; AI returns one or more Dox commands and executes them immediately
usage.? switch language to English: Typically generates and runs set Config.Lang en-US
usage.? check path then list files: May generate and run pwd; ls (multi-commands separated by semicolon)
usage.? show my local IP configuration: May generate and run cmd ipconfig (AI-generated cmd must carry a concrete command)

usage.chat [question]: Single-turn Q&A; AI can call Dox tools via tool protocol before answering
usage.chat: Enter interactive chat mode (type exit or quit to leave)
usage.chat what files are in current directory: AI may trigger tools like ls/ll/pwd/help/path/env/cd and then summarize
usage.chat how many python processes are runni: AI may call the cmd tool to run a system command (e.g. cmd tasklist) and then summarize

usage.& serve [device_name]: Start listening in the current terminal to join the LAN cluster as a controlled node (default name is 'node')
usage.& stop: Stop the LAN listening service in the current terminal
usage.& scan: Send a UDP broadcast to scan all Dox nodes in the LAN that have enabled 'serve' and list their IPs and ports
usage.& send <device_name> [-q] <command>: Send a single command to a specified Dox node via TCP. By default, the remote node outputs the execution synchronously. Add '-q' for quiet/silent execution
usage.& connect <device_name> [-q]: Enter immersive remote control mode. Type 'exit' or '& disconnect' to quit. Add '-q' for quiet execution on the target node during this session

usage.ll: List files in detail (same as ls -l)

usage.cat [file_name]: Print the entire content of a file
usage.cat [file_name] -head [lines]: Print the first few lines of the file (or use -l instead)
usage.cat [file_name] -tail [lines]: Print the last few lines of the file

usage.version: Display version number and release date

usage.video [video path] --fps 15: Override playback FPS (lower can reduce lag)

usage.img [image path]: Render an image in low resolution (fit to terminal)

usage.download [URL] [save path]: Download a file to the specified path

usage.rm [file...]: Remove one or more files (asks for confirmation)

usage.set [key] [value]: Update root config in config.json (dot path supported, e.g. Config.Lang); system variables refresh immediately after writing

usage.path add [dir] --all: Add to both persistent and temporary PATH
usage.path rm [dir] --all: Remove from both persistent and temporary

usage.env: List all variables grouped as temporary, persistent and system
usage.env list [-t|-p|-s|--all]: List variables by scope (-t temp / -p persist / -s system / --all)
usage.env [NAME]: Show a variable value and its source (same as env get [NAME])
usage.env set [NAME] [value]: Set a temporary variable (this session only)
usage.env set [NAME] [value] -s: Write a system variable (updates config.json and refreshes)
usage.env refresh: Reload config.json and path.json to refresh system and persistent variables
usage.env set PATH [dir] -p: Append a directory to persistent PATH (same as path add [dir] -p)
usage.env path: Show effective PATH (same as path show)
usage.Note: System variables come from config.json and load at startup; user variables are added via env/path. Priority: temp > persist > system > process environment
